title: Past-Due Premium for a Grace-Cure Payment: Premium Billing Accounts Computation
content:
**Definition.** On Premium Billing Accounts, the grace-cure payment is the premium past due on the account for the coverage months that have begun, never less than 0.00 and rounded half up to the cent once, on the final figure.

**The premium past due for the coverage months that have begun** is:
- every invoice the account carries,
- plus every returned payment and every refund,
- less every payment received and every premium credit booked,

leaving out returned-payment fees, and leaving out the invoice issued last when its coverage month has not yet begun. Of two invoices issued on the same day, the one recorded first counts as issued last. A coverage month has begun once the payment date falls in that month or later.

**Ledger items and their treatment**
| Ledger item | Treatment |
|---|---|
| invoice (any, including the invoice issued last when its month has begun) | added |
| invoice issued last, coverage month not yet begun | left out |
| returned payment | added |
| refund issued | added |
| payment received | subtracted |
| premium credit | subtracted |
| returned-payment fee | left out |

**Worked example (hypothetical ledger, payment date in October).** Invoices for August (61.40), September (61.40) and October (61.40), plus an invoice for November (61.40) issued last; one payment of 61.40 received, later returned (returned payment 61.40); a returned-payment fee of 25.00; a premium credit of 7.15.
Invoices with begun months: 184.20. Plus the returned payment: 245.60. Less the payment: 184.20. Less the credit: 177.05. The November invoice (month not yet begun) and the fee are left out. Grace-cure payment: 177.05.
